title: Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana: Rs 2,500/Month Apply
meta_description: Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana gives Jharkhand women Rs 2,500/month via DBT. Check eligibility, status at mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in. Helpline: 18008900215.

hero.one_liner: Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana gives women in Jharkhand Rs 2,500 a month by DBT. Launched August 2024, for women aged 21 to 50.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana (abbreviated MMMSY) is a flagship welfare scheme launched in August 2024 by the Jharkhand state government under Chief Minister Hemant Soren, providing Rs 2,500 per month as direct financial assistance to eligible women across the state. The scheme recognises the economic contribution of women to their households and gives them a regular income stream they can use independently.

The word Maiya (also written as Maiyya or Maaiya) is a term of endearment and respect for women, particularly mothers and elder women, in the dialects spoken across Jharkhand's tribal and non-tribal communities. By naming the scheme Maiya Samman, which means respect or honour for the Maiya, the Jharkhand government signals that the benefit is not charity but an acknowledgement of women's dignity and their rightful claim to state support.

eligibility_filters.notes: Women aged 21-50, permanent residents of Jharkhand, family income up to Rs 1 lakh, Aadhaar-linked bank account. Rs 2,500 a month by DBT (raised from Rs 1,000). Apply at mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in. Excludes government employees, pensioners, and taxpayers.

how_to_apply.title: Confirm eligibility
how_to_apply.description: Check that you meet all criteria: you are a woman aged 21-50, a permanent resident of Jharkhand, you hold a Pink/Yellow/White/Green ration card, your annual family income is below Rs 8 lakh, and you have an Aadhaar-linked bank account in your own name. If your bank account is not yet Aadhaar-seeded, visit your bank branch to complete this first.

how_to_apply.title: Apply online at mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in
how_to_apply.description: Visit mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in, click on the apply link, and fill in the application form with your Aadhaar number, ration card number, bank account details, age, and address. Upload your Aadhaar card, ration card, and bank passbook (or cancelled cheque), then submit and save the reference number for tracking.

how_to_apply.title: Apply offline at CSC or Gram Panchayat
how_to_apply.description: If you cannot apply online, visit a local Common Service Centre (CSC/Jan Seva Kendra), Gram Panchayat office, or Block office, carrying your original Aadhaar card, ration card, bank passbook, and passport-size photo. The CSC operator will fill and submit the application on your behalf and provide a printed acknowledgement with your reference number.

how_to_apply.title: Track your application status
how_to_apply.description: Go to mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in and use the Status Check section by entering your Aadhaar number or application reference number. You can see whether your application is pending, approved, or rejected; if rejected, the reason is displayed so you can correct the issue and re-apply.

how_to_apply.title: Receive Rs 2,500 monthly via DBT
how_to_apply.description: Once approved, Rs 2,500 is credited to your Aadhaar-linked bank account each month; verify receipt via your passbook, mobile banking app, or SMS. For payment-related issues, call the helpline at 18008900215.

ministry: Department of Women, Child Development and Social Security, Jharkhand

extra_sections.heading: What Maiya Samman Yojana Is
content: The monthly benefit of Rs 2,500 translates to Rs 30,000 per year, which for many rural women in Jharkhand represents a significant and reliable supplementary income. In a state with high poverty rates and large tribal populations, Rs 2,500 per month can cover a household's monthly expenditure on essential groceries, medicines, children's school fees, or small business inputs.

To be eligible for Maiya Samman Yojana, a woman must be a permanent resident of Jharkhand and must be between 21 and 50 years of age at the time of application. The age ceiling of 50 years distinguishes this scheme from old-age pension schemes, which typically begin at 60 years; women above 50 in Jharkhand may instead be covered under the Sarvajan Pension Yojana once they turn 60.

The scheme is income-linked: the annual family income must be below Rs 8 lakh. This Rs 8 lakh ceiling is notably broader than many comparable women's welfare schemes in other states, reflecting Jharkhand's intent to cover a wide segment of its women population including lower-middle-income households, not just those classified as BPL.

Ration card possession is a key eligibility condition: women holding Pink, Yellow, White, or Green ration cards issued by the Jharkhand state or the central government are eligible. These cards are those issued under the National Food Security Act or Jharkhand's state food schemes, meaning the scheme targets families already present in the PDS beneficiary database.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The bank account must be Aadhaar-linked for DBT to work, so women who have not yet seeded their account should visit their bank branch before applying for Maiya Samman. The benefit amount is transferred directly to the woman's own bank account rather than a shared family account, ensuring the money is within her direct control.

The application process for Maiya Samman Yojana is managed through the official portal mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in, where women can apply online, check their application status, and verify their payment history. Offline applications can also be submitted at local government offices, Gram Panchayat offices, and Common Service Centres for women who do not have personal internet access.

After submission, the application goes through a verification process where the eligibility criteria (age, residency, ration card, income) are checked against the state's database. Once verified and approved, the woman is added to the beneficiary list and begins receiving Rs 2,500 per month, with payments arriving on a monthly cycle consistent with similar income support schemes in other states.

The Maiya Samman helpline number is 18008900215, which is a toll-free number that beneficiaries can call for help with the application process, status inquiries, payment-related questions, or to report technical issues with the portal. The helpline is particularly useful for women in rural areas who may have submitted offline applications and need to track progress.

extra_sections.title: Rs 2,500 a Month, Raised From Rs 1,000
extra_sections.content:
Launched in August 2024 by CM Hemant Soren, the scheme first paid Rs 1,000 a month, then was raised to Rs 2,500. The money goes straight to the woman's bank account.

That is Rs 30,000 a year, paid by DBT, for women aged 21 to 50 whose family income is within the limit.

extra_sections.heading: The Income and Residence Rules
content: The scheme status for an existing applicant can also be checked online at mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in by entering the Aadhaar number or the application reference number. Applicants who have been approved but are not receiving payments can verify their bank account linking status on the portal, since an un-seeded or mismatched Aadhaar-bank record is the most common reason for payment failures in DBT schemes.

Jharkhand has one of the highest proportions of tribal populations among all Indian states, with Scheduled Tribes comprising over 26% of the state's population. Many women from Santali, Oraon, Munda, and Ho tribal communities are ration card holders and thus eligible for Maiya Samman, and the scheme directly addresses their economic marginalization through a reliable monthly income.

Women who receive certain other government schemes are not automatically disqualified from Maiya Samman unless they belong to excluded categories such as government employees, income taxpayers, or those with incomes above Rs 8 lakh. A woman who also receives a BOCW labour benefit may still be eligible for Maiya Samman if she meets the age and ration card criteria.

The excluded categories under Maiya Samman Yojana typically include women who are central or state government employees or pensioners, women who pay income tax, and elected representatives at any level of government. Women in these categories are considered to have adequate financial resources and are therefore excluded from this welfare benefit.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply
content: Maiya Samman was announced in 2024 as part of a broader welfare package that included the Abua Awas housing scheme, the Abua Swasthya Suraksha health card, and continuation of the Sarvajan Pension. The combined impact of these four schemes addresses multiple dimensions of poverty for Jharkhand's most vulnerable families, covering shelter, health, income support, and old-age security simultaneously.

Documents typically required for the Maiya Samman application include the Aadhaar card, the ration card (Pink/Yellow/White/Green), proof of bank account with Aadhaar linkage (passbook or cancelled cheque), and a passport-size photograph. Women applying offline at CSC or Gram Panchayat offices should carry original copies of these documents for the verification process.

New applications are processed in batches, so a woman may wait 2-6 weeks after submission before receiving her first monthly payment, after which Rs 2,500 continues automatically as long as eligibility remains unchanged. If any eligibility condition changes (for example, if family income rises above Rs 8 lakh), the benefit may be suspended following periodic database reviews.

For women living in remote tribal areas of Jharkhand such as Latehar, Gumla, Simdega, and Khunti districts, where banking access can be challenging, the Jharkhand government has worked with Business Correspondents and bank mitras to facilitate Aadhaar-bank seeding and the application process. Village-level camps have been organised to enroll women and resolve common application hurdles in these underserved areas.

extra_sections.heading: How the Payment Reaches You
content: At Rs 2,500 per month, Maiya Samman is among the higher-value women's income support schemes in India, placing it ahead of Karnataka's Gruha Lakshmi (Rs 2,000) and Tamil Nadu's Kalaignar Magalir Urimai (Rs 1,000). The broad Rs 8 lakh income ceiling widens the reach significantly compared with schemes in other states that use Rs 1.5 lakh or Rs 2.5 lakh ceilings.

Self-Help Groups (SHGs) affiliated with JSLPS (Jharkhand State Livelihood Promotion Society) have played a significant role in spreading awareness about Maiya Samman among rural and tribal women. SHG meetings at the village level are used to explain eligibility, guide members through the application process, and follow up on pending applications or payment delays on behalf of beneficiaries.

The appeal mechanism for rejected applications involves submitting a representation to the Block Development Officer or the District Social Welfare Office with supporting documents explaining why the rejection was incorrect. If a woman believes she was wrongly excluded from the beneficiary list, she can escalate through the district administration, and the helpline at 18008900215 can help identify the correct escalation authority.

Maiya Samman Yojana is implemented and monitored by the Jharkhand state government's Women and Child Development Department in coordination with the Food and Civil Supplies Department (for ration card verification) and the Finance Department (for DBT transfers). This multi-department coordination ensures that both the eligibility check and the payment transfer are grounded in reliable state databases, reducing duplication and leakage.

extra_sections.heading: If a Payment Is Missed
content: Periodic deduplication exercises are conducted to remove ineligible beneficiaries from the list, for example those who have since joined a government job, whose income has crossed Rs 8 lakh, or whose ration card status has changed. Women removed after a deduplication review are notified through their registered mobile number and can appeal within a stipulated period if they believe the removal was incorrect.

The Jharkhand government has positioned Maiya Samman as a step toward achieving financial independence for women, alongside other SHG-based livelihood programs. The monthly Rs 2,500 provides a predictable cash inflow that women can use as seed capital for SHG savings, as collateral for small microfinance loans, or as working capital for household-level microenterprises such as poultry, tailoring, or vegetable vending.

extra_sections.title: Paid Directly to Her Account
extra_sections.desc:
The money is sent by DBT to the woman's own Aadhaar-linked bank account, not a family member's.

Keep your Aadhaar seeded to the bank, or the transfer can fail even after approval. Check your status on the portal if a month is missed.

extra_sections.heading: If a Payment Is Missed More
content: Women with disabilities who are between 21 and 50 years of age and meet the ration card and income criteria are also eligible for Maiya Samman Yojana. The scheme does not have a separate sub-category for differently-abled women in this age group, but they can apply through the standard process; women with disabilities above 50 years can additionally seek coverage under the Sarvajan Pension's disability category.

The integration of Maiya Samman payments with the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) bank accounts has been a significant enabler for women in Jharkhand who previously had no bank account. Many women opened Jan Dhan accounts specifically to receive the Maiya Samman DBT, which has had the secondary benefit of bringing them into the formal banking system for the first time.

extra_sections.heading: How the Scheme Helps Families
content: Gram Sabha (village assembly) sessions held at the Panchayat level have been used to both publicise Maiya Samman Yojana and to conduct on-the-spot eligibility verification in rural areas. During these camps, bank account seeding, Aadhaar authentication, and form submission can all happen in one session, which reduces the number of trips a rural woman needs to make to a block office or bank branch.

The Maiya Samman portal at mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in also allows beneficiaries to update their bank account details if they have changed the account linked to their Aadhaar. This is important because a DBT transfer to a closed or incorrect account will fail and the payment is lost until the account details are corrected; beneficiaries should update their details promptly after any bank account change.

extra_sections.title: Payment Not Received This Month?
extra_sections.content:
First check that your Aadhaar is still seeded to your bank account, since a broken link is the most common reason.

Then check your status on mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in or raise it at the nearest block office with your application number.

extra_sections.heading: How the Scheme Helps Families More
content: For women who belong to primitive tribal groups (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups or PVTGs) in Jharkhand such as the Birhor, Asur, and Korwa communities, the Maiya Samman scheme has been promoted through special outreach drives by the Tribal Welfare Department. These outreach drives recognise that PVTG women are less likely to have documents in order and need additional support to complete the enrollment process.

The minimum age of 21 years for Maiya Samman eligibility coincides roughly with the legal age of majority and is designed to ensure that benefits go to women who are managing households, not to adolescent girls who are covered under separate schemes such as the Savitribai Phule Kishori Samridhi Yojana for girls in Jharkhand. This age segmentation ensures that each age group of women has a relevant government program addressing their specific needs.

extra_sections.text: Pehle ghar ke liye paiso ke liye pati par nirbhar rehna padta tha. Ab Maiya Samman ke Rs 2,500 apne haath mein aate hain toh bacchon ki school fees aur ration dono mil jaata hai.

extra_sections.heading: Maiya Samman in Context
content: Research on cash transfer programs for women in India has consistently shown that when women control regular cash income, household spending on food, education, and healthcare improves. Maiya Samman Yojana is designed with this evidence in mind: by crediting money directly into the woman's individual bank account, the scheme ensures she is the decision-maker for how the funds are used, rather than the funds passing through a male household head.

Women who shift residence within Jharkhand after enrollment do not need to re-apply for Maiya Samman, as the benefit is linked to the woman's Aadhaar number rather than to a specific village or block. However, if a woman relocates to another state, she becomes ineligible since the scheme is specific to Jharkhand's ration card holders and state residents.

extra_sections.heading: Maiya Samman in Context More
content: The Maiya Samman beneficiary list is published at the Gram Panchayat level and is also accessible on the scheme's official portal, allowing community members to verify that eligible women have been included and to flag cases where eligible women have been left out. This transparency measure is part of the Jharkhand government's broader commitment to open and verifiable welfare delivery.

For women in Jharkhand who face domestic financial constraints or whose male family members historically controlled household income, the monthly Rs 2,500 from Maiya Samman arriving directly in their bank account creates a meaningful shift in bargaining power within the household. When money lands in a woman's own account, she gains a degree of financial autonomy and household spending authority that is very difficult to achieve through non-cash support or in-kind transfers alone.

extra_sections.title: What to Keep in Mind Notes
extra_sections.content: Economic researchers and development economists studying cash transfer programs in India have consistently documented marked improvements in women's agency, mobility, and decision-making authority when they hold independent regular income. Maiya Samman thus functions both as a welfare scheme and as a structural intervention in gender equity, giving women across one of India's more economically disadvantaged states a predictable, independently controlled financial resource they can rightly call entirely their own.

faqs.question: What is Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana?
faqs.answer: Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana (MMMSY) is a Jharkhand government scheme launched in August 2024 that gives eligible women Rs 2,500 per month (Rs 30,000 per year) directly into their Aadhaar-linked bank account via DBT. It covers women aged 21-50 who are permanent Jharkhand residents with a ration card and annual family income below Rs 8 lakh.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Maiya Samman Yojana?
faqs.answer: Women aged 21 to 50 years who are permanent residents of Jharkhand, hold a Pink, Yellow, White, or Green ration card, have an annual family income below Rs 8 lakh, and have an Aadhaar-linked bank account are eligible. Government employees, income taxpayers, and elected representatives are typically excluded.

faqs.question: How much money does Maiya Samman give per month?
faqs.answer: Rs 2,500 per month, which equals Rs 30,000 per year. The amount is transferred directly to the woman's Aadhaar-linked bank account each month via DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer).

faqs.question: How do I apply for Maiya Samman Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Apply online at mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in with your Aadhaar, ration card, and bank account details. You can also apply offline at your local CSC, Gram Panchayat office, or Block office with original documents.

After applying, you receive an application reference number to track status.

faqs.question: How do I check my Maiya Samman Yojana status?
faqs.answer:
Visit mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in and enter your Aadhaar number or application reference number in the Status Check section. You can see if your application is pending, approved, or rejected.

For help, call the helpline at 18008900215.

faqs.question: What ration card is required for Maiya Samman Yojana?
faqs.answer: Women holding Pink, Yellow, White, or Green ration cards issued by the Jharkhand state or under the National Food Security Act are eligible. These are the standard PDS ration card categories in Jharkhand.

faqs.question: Is Maiya Samman available for women above 50 years?
faqs.answer: No. The scheme covers women between 21 and 50 years of age only. Women above 50 years may be eligible for the Sarvajan Pension Yojana once they turn 60 (old-age pension category) or for the widow pension category if applicable.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for Maiya Samman Yojana?
faqs.answer: The annual family income must be below Rs 8 lakh. This is a relatively broad ceiling, making the scheme accessible to a large proportion of Jharkhand women including lower-middle-income households, not just those with BPL cards.

faqs.question: What is the Maiya Samman Yojana helpline number?
faqs.answer:
The toll-free helpline is 18008900215. Call for help with applying, checking application status, payment issues, or any other queries about the scheme.

You can also visit the official portal mmmsy.jharkhand.gov.in.

faqs.question: Can I get Maiya Samman if I also receive another government benefit?
faqs.answer: Receiving certain other government benefits may not automatically disqualify you, as long as you are not a government employee or income taxpayer and your income stays below Rs 8 lakh. Confirm with your Block office or the scheme helpline whether your specific combination of benefits is permitted.
